  "body": "# Description

We've had a lot of different issues and PRs related to arg handling with externals since the rewrite of `run-external` in #12921:

- #12950
- #12955
- #13000
- #13001
- #13021
- #13027
- #13028
- #13073

Many of these are caused by the argument handling of external calls and `run-external` being very special and involving the parser handing quoted strings over to `run-external` so that it knows whether to expand tildes and globs and so on. This is really unusual and also makes it harder to use `run-external`, and also harder to understand it (and probably is part of the reason why it was rewritten in the first place).

part.text:
Fixed. Summary:

**Root cause:** In `crates/nu-command/src/system/run_external.rs`, external command args get tilde/glob expanded. For `git add .`, the glob of `.` resolves to `<cwd>/.`, and `Path::strip_prefix(cwd)` normalizes away the `.` component, yielding an empty string, which was then passed to git (`fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec`).

**Fix** (crates/nu-command/src/system/run_external.rs:334-344): when stripping PWD from a glob result leaves an empty path, fall back to `.` instead — matching upstream nushell PR #12950.

**Validation:**
- `cargo test -p nu-command --lib system::run_external` — 5/5 pass
- `cargo test --test main` — 1234 passed, 0 failed (includes the FAIL_TO_PASS test `pass_dot_as_external_arguments`, which now passes; confirmed stable across repeated runs)
- End-to-end: created a repo in a container, ran `nu -c "git add ."` → file staged successfully
